title: Signal consolidator for incidents with PagerDuty quick-actions and Slack actionable summaries
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
Our current incident integrations emit many small, noisy PD/Slack notifications for single root causes because traces, metrics, and log alerts are sent independently. Responders spend cycles context-switching across channels and manually assembling evidence. We need a consolidation layer that groups correlated signals into a single responder payload and surfaces high-value artifacts (trace snippets, metric spike graphs, recent KV cache snapshot links, relevant rollouts) with actionable quick actions in PagerDuty and Slack.

Goal:
Deliver a service- and console-level feature that: (1) ingests observability signals (traces, metric anomalies, log error spikes) and correlates them into a single incident signal; (2) enriches the signal with a concise evidence bundle (2–3 trace snippets, top error logs, token-latency heatmap link); (3) posts a consolidated PagerDuty event and a Slack thread with structured summary + operator quick-actions (snooze PD, attach runbook section, trigger model fallback or traffic-shift); (4) auto-create a postmortem skeleton in Confluence/Drive when severity exceeds threshold.

Non-goal:
This ticket is not the full long-term dedupe engine across all customers or a replacement for external SIEM correlation. Focus on Redwood-hosted incidents (hosted + dedicated) and enable private deployments in a follow-up iteration.
acceptance_criteria:
- A consolidation service prototype runs in staging and receives simulated traces, metric alerts, and log spikes, producing a single PD event instead of three independent events.
- The PD event contains: severity score, top-3 trace snippets with links to the full trace, top error log lines, and a link to a console evidence bundle.
- Slack thread created in the incident channel with a structured summary card and three quick-actions visible as buttons: Snooze (15/60/240m), Attach runbook (open chooser modal), Trigger fallback (invoke a safe rollback/fallback lambda).
- Postmortem skeleton auto-created for incidents >= severity 2 with prefilled fields (timeline, signals, initial hypothesis) and a link in the PD/Slack payload.
- End-to-end tests validate dedupe behavior for correlated and uncorrelated signals.
- Metrics: reduce duplicate PD incidents by >= 60% for simulated correlated signals, and average responder context-assembly time reduced by >= 45% in the simulation harness.
design_notes:
High-level design:
1) Signal Ingest Bus: lightweight Kafka topic or internal event bus that normalizes incoming signals to a canonical IncidentSignal schema (signal_id, timestamp, source_type, fingerprint_hash, severity_vector).
2) Correlation Engine: sliding window correlation with fingerprint hashing (trace span id prefixes + metric name + error signature) and adaptive windowing based on signal types. Scoring heuristic combines recency, shared trace/span IDs, and dynamic weight for customer SLA.
3) Evidence Assembler: select representative trace snippets (bounded to 3 spans), snapshot of relevant metrics (last 5 minutes), top log lines, KV cache snapshot link. We will store assembled evidence as a signed, time-limited bundle in S3 for hosted and a console link for private configs.
4) Actionability Layer: PD adapter (RFC to PD V3 alerts) with attachments + actions; Slack adapter that posts a compact Block Kit message with buttons wired to the Console action API.
5) Postmortem seed: when severity >= threshold, call postmortem service to create skeleton doc using a template and attach evidence links.

Trade-offs:
- Aggressive dedupe window reduces noise but risks delaying unrelated incidents colliding in time. We'll expose window sizes to config and default conservative values.
- Keeping evidence bundles in S3 simplifies hosted flow but requires work for private deployments (local storage or signed proxy).

Privacy/security:
- Evidence bundles must be access-controlled and signed; PD attachments should not contain raw PHI/logs. We'll redact PII with existing log-redaction rules before assembly.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2 sprints):
- Build lightweight Signal Ingest Bus and canonical schema (ENG-102346 will own schema).
- Implement prototype Correlation Engine with simple fingerprint rules (trace span prefix + metric name).
- Evidence Assembler: basic trace snippet extractor and S3 bundle writer (hosted only).
- PD adapter: send single PD event with JSON payload and link to evidence.
- Slack adapter: post Block Kit summary with three action buttons wired to mock endpoints.

Phase 2 (2 sprints):
- Improve heuristics, add metric spike detection, adjust scoring weights.
- Implement runbook chooser flow and Postmortem skeleton creation.
- Add safety checks for quick-actions (rate limits, auth checks).
- End-to-end tests and load testing with synthetic incidents.

Phase 3 (follow-up):
- Private deployment storage adapter, RBAC for evidence access, prod rollouts and telemetry-driven tuning.
rollout_plan:
- Feature gated behind "incident-consolidation" feature flag per org.
- Start with internal Redwood org + partner Beta (10 customers) for 2 weeks, collect responder feedback.
- Expand to all hosted tenants with low-traffic windows and monitor dedupe and false-grouping metrics.
- Enable private deployment path after storage adapter is implemented.
- Gradual PD action enablement: first only Snooze and Attach Runbook (low-risk), then add Trigger Fallback after safety review.
metrics:
- Duplicate PD incidents prevented (count)
- Time to assemble evidence (median seconds)
- Percentage of incidents that auto-generate postmortem skeletons
- False-grouping rate (operators mark an incident as incorrectly merged)
- Average time to resolution for incidents handled using quick-actions vs baseline
- Telemetry: correlation window utilizations and scoring distribution
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for canonical schema and evidence redaction.
- Integration tests: simulated traces+metrics+logs feed through ingest bus and assert single PD event emitted for correlated inputs.
- Load test: two-hour stair-step with 1000 signals/min to validate latency of consolidation (target < 2s additional latency).
- Chaos tests: inject unrelated signals during high traffic to validate dedupe conservatism.
- Security tests: validate redaction rules and signed-bundle expiry enforcement.
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: incorrect dedupe merges unrelated incidents. Mitigation: conservative default windows, operator undo (split incident) action in Console and Slack, and telemetry to track false-groupings.
- Risk: Quick-action causes unintended side-effects (e.g., wrong rollback). Mitigation: require two-step confirmation for destructive actions and RBAC checks; start with low-risk actions.
- Risk: PII leakage in evidence bundles. Mitigation: reuse log-redaction pipeline and require security review before enabling for regulated customers.
